newsitem.title: USA: US late spot gasoline slips on NYMEX, lower diffs.
newsitem.headline: US late spot gasoline slips on NYMEX, lower diffs.

text.p: U.S. spot gasoline prices fell sharply by late Tuesday from lower NYMEX values and mostly weaker differentials as traders cited more-than plentiful supplies in New York Harbor and the Gulf Coast, traders said.

The market was otherwise bereft of much direction, one Gulf trader said, speculating the lackluster environment could be repeated Wednesday because of a postponement of weekly API data that had been expected late Tuesday.
The API was unable to confirm when the data -- delayed because of a computer glitch -- would be released. It said a new release time would be announced Wednesday.
"The midcontinent is sloppy right now, and that's backing barrels into the Gulf," one gasoline trader said.
Prompt Gulf Coast unleaded M2 gasoline was sold for 4.25 cents below the April print, 0.40 cent weaker than Monday, traders said, with reformulated "A2" grade easing slightly to 2.50 cents under.

"It was a dead-quiet market. All the products are oversupplied except low-sulfur distillates," one Gulf trader said. "Gasoline and heating oil are particularly oversupplied. I think they're heading lower."
